title: Prototype GPU acceleration for belief propagation
description:
Prototype a HIP/ROCm GPU acceleration wave for coding workloads and decide, from measured evidence, whether LDPC BP and BCH syndrome evaluation should move toward production GPU backends.

## Background

The current epic mixes newer HIP/ROCm work with older Vulkan/GLSL tasks and a downstream production-backend epic. The confirmed direction for this epic is HIP/ROCm only, using the existing `gf2-kernels-hip` unsafe-isolation pattern. The epic covers a prototype and feasibility decision, not production backend rollout.

The target evidence environment is AMD RX 6950 XT / `gfx1030` with ROCm 7.2 and `hipcc` at `/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc`. GPU performance claims compare against the best existing production CPU path at the same batch or campaign shape, including rayon where production uses rayon.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] The epic uses HIP/ROCm as the only GPU backend direction; Vulkan/GLSL children are rewritten or closed as superseded.
- [hard] LDPC BP has a HIP prototype with CPU/GPU correctness evidence and at least 3x speedup versus the best production CPU path at the selected design workload.
- [hard] BCH syndrome evaluation has a HIP prototype with exact CPU/GPU syndrome equivalence and at least 5x speedup versus the best production CPU path at the selected design workload.
- [hard] Shared HIP scheduling work quantifies direct per-thread/default-stream submission versus a shared scheduler and demonstrates measurable end-to-end throughput improvement.
- [hard] The final feasibility report states go/investigate/abandon for LDPC BP and BCH syndrome evaluation, with raw evidence paths and downstream production recommendations.
- [hard] Default workspace CI remains green without ROCm installed; HIP-only checks are isolated to the `gf2-kernels-hip` crate or `gf2-coding --features hip` on ROCm hosts.
- [hard] No unsafe code leaks outside `gf2-kernels-hip`.

## Notes

Spec doc: `dev/plans/hip_gpu_prototype_wave.md`.

Non-goals: Vulkan/GLSL, CUDA, production multi-backend selection, and production GPU backend rollout for all code types. Production work remains downstream of this prototype epic's final decision.
